translations.idiomatic: Jing had earlier agreed with Gao Huan that when he received a letter, a slight dot on the back meant he should come.

sentences.zh: 書至，無點，景不至。

translations.literal: The letter arrived without a dot, and Jing did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The letter arrived without a dot, and Jing did not come.

sentences.zh: 又聞神武疾，遂擁兵自固。

translations.literal: He also heard that Shenwu was ill and thereupon gathered troops to hold himself secure.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard that Gao Huan was ill and thereupon gathered troops and fortified himself.

sentences.zh: 神武謂世子曰：「我雖疾，爾面更有餘憂色，何也？

translations.literal: Shenwu said to the heir: "Though I am ill, your face still shows extra worry — why?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said to the heir, "Though I am ill, your face still shows extra worry — why?

sentences.zh: 」世子未對。

translations.literal: " The heir did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The heir did not answer.

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「豈非憂侯景叛耶？

translations.literal: He asked again: "Is it not worry that Hou Jing will rebel?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "Is it worry that Hou Jing will rebel?

translations.literal: " He said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「景專制河南十四年矣，常有飛揚跋扈志，顧我能養，豈為汝駕御也！

translations.literal: Shenwu said: "Jing has monopolized Henan for fourteen years; he has always had a proud and overbearing will, but submitted because I could support him — how could he be driven for you!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Jing has monopolized Henan for fourteen years; he has always had a proud and overbearing will, but submitted because I could support him — how could he be driven for you!

sentences.zh: 今四方未定，勿遽發哀。

translations.literal: The four quarters are not yet settled — do not hastily announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The four quarters are not yet settled — do not hastily announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 厙狄干鮮卑老公，斛律金勑勒老公，並性遒直，終不負汝。

translations.literal: Kudigan Gan, the Xianbei old fellow, and Hulü Jin, the Chile old fellow, are both upright by nature and will never fail you.
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan Gan, the Xianbei old fellow, and Hulü Jin, the Chile old fellow, are both upright by nature and will never fail you.

sentences.zh: 可朱渾道元、劉豐生遠來投我，必無異心。

translations.literal: Kezhuhun Daoyuan and Liu Fengsheng came from afar to join me — they will surely have no different heart.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhuhun Daoyuan and Liu Fengsheng came from afar to join me — they will surely have no different heart.

sentences.zh: 賀拔焉過兒樸實無罪過。

translations.literal: Heba Yanguo'er is plain and without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yanguo'er is plain and without fault.

sentences.zh: 潘樂本作道人，心和厚，汝兄弟當得其力。

translations.literal: Pan Le was originally a Daoist; his heart is kind and generous — your brothers should gain strength from him.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Le was originally a Daoist; his heart is kind and generous — your brothers should gain strength from him.

sentences.zh: 韓軌少戇，宜寬借之。

translations.literal: Han Gui is somewhat dull — you should treat him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gui is somewhat dull — you should treat him leniently.

sentences.zh: 彭樂心腹難得，宜防護之。

translations.literal: Peng Le is hard to read at heart — you should guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Le is hard to read at heart — you should guard against him.

sentences.zh: 少堪敵侯景者唯有慕容紹宗，我故不貴之，留以與汝，宜深加殊禮，委以經略。」

translations.literal: Of those who can barely match Hou Jing there is only Murong Shaozong; I therefore did not promote him highly and left him for you — you should grant him exceptional honors and entrust him with strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Of those who can barely match Hou Jing there is only Murong Shaozong; I therefore did not promote him highly and left him for you — you should grant him exceptional honors and entrust him with strategy."

sentences.zh: 神武性深密高岸，終日儼然，人不能測。

translations.literal: Shenwu's nature was deep, secretive, and lofty; all day long he remained stern, and men could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's nature was deep, secretive, and lofty; all day long he remained stern, and men could not fathom him.

sentences.zh: 機權之際，變化若神。

translations.literal: At moments of stratagem he changed like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: At moments of stratagem he changed like a spirit.

sentences.zh: 至於軍國大略，獨運懷抱，文武將吏罕有預之。

translations.literal: As for the great designs of army and state, he carried them alone in his breast, and civil and military officers rarely shared in them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the great designs of army and state, he carried them alone in his breast, and civil and military officers rarely shared in them.

sentences.zh: 統馭軍衆，法令嚴肅，臨敵制勝，策出無方。

translations.literal: In commanding armies his laws were strict and solemn; facing the enemy he prevailed, and his stratagems came from nowhere fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In commanding armies his laws were strict and solemn; facing the enemy he prevailed, and his stratagems came from nowhere fixed.

sentences.zh: 聽斷昭察，不可欺犯。

translations.literal: In hearing cases he was clear-sighted and could not be deceived or offended.
translations.idiomatic: In hearing cases he was clear-sighted and could not be deceived or offended.

sentences.zh: 知人好士，全護勳舊。

translations.literal: He knew men and loved scholars, and fully protected those of merit and old service.
translations.idiomatic: He knew men and loved scholars, and fully protected those of merit and old service.

sentences.zh: 性周給，每有文教，常殷勤款悉，指事論心，不尚綺靡。

translations.literal: By nature he was thorough and considerate; whenever he issued a civil edict he was always earnest and detailed, speaking to the matter and to the heart, and did not prize ornate language.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was thorough and considerate; whenever he issued a civil edict he was always earnest and detailed, speaking to the matter and to the heart, and did not prize ornate language.

sentences.zh: 擢人授任，在於得才，苟其所堪，乃至拔於廝養，有虛聲無實者，稀見任用。

translations.literal: In raising men and granting office what mattered was obtaining talent; if a man was capable, he might even be pulled up from stable service, while those with empty reputation and no substance were rarely employed.
translations.idiomatic: In raising men and granting office what mattered was obtaining talent; if a man was capable, he might even be pulled up from stable service, while those with empty reputation and no substance were rarely employed.

sentences.zh: 諸將出討，奉行方略，罔不克捷，違失指畫，多致奔亡。

translations.literal: When generals went out on campaign and followed his plans, none failed to win; when they missed his design, many came to ruin and flight.
translations.idiomatic: When generals went out on campaign and followed his plans, none failed to win; when they missed his design, many came to ruin and flight.

sentences.zh: 雅尚儉素，刀劍鞍勒無金玉之飾。

translations.literal: He naturally favored simplicity; swords, saddles, and bridles had no ornament of gold or jade.
translations.idiomatic: He naturally favored simplicity; swords, saddles, and bridles had no ornament of gold or jade.

sentences.zh: 少能劇飲，自當大任，不過三爵。

translations.literal: In youth he could drink heavily, but once he took great responsibility he never passed three cups.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he could drink heavily, but once he took great responsibility he never passed three cups.

sentences.zh: 居家如官。

translations.literal: At home he was as at office.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was as at office.

sentences.zh: 仁恕愛士。

translations.literal: He was humane, forgiving, and loving toward scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He was humane, forgiving, and loving toward scholars.

sentences.zh: 始，范陽盧景裕以明經稱，魯郡韓毅以工書顯，咸以謀逆見擒，並蒙恩置之第館，教授諸子。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Fanyang Lu Jingyu was famed for mastery of the classics and Lu Commandery Han Yi for skill in calligraphy; both were seized on charges of plotting rebellion, yet both received grace and were housed in his residence to instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, Fanyang Lu Jingyu was famed for mastery of the classics and Lu Commandery Han Yi for skill in calligraphy; both were seized on charges of plotting rebellion, yet both received grace and were housed in his residence to instruct his sons.

sentences.zh: 其文武之士盡節所事，見執獲而不罪者甚多。

translations.literal: Many civil and military men who had served their lords to the utmost, once captured, were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Many civil and military men who had served their lords to the utmost, once captured, were not punished.

sentences.zh: 故遐邇歸心，皆思效力。

translations.literal: Therefore near and far gave him their hearts, and all wished to serve him with effort.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore near and far gave him their hearts, and all wished to serve him with effort.

sentences.zh: 至南威梁國，北懷蠕蠕，吐谷渾、阿至羅咸所招納，獲其力用，規略遠矣。

translations.literal: To the south he awed Liang, to the north he won over the Rouran, and the Tuyuhun and Azhiluo were all brought in by his summons; he gained their strength for use — his design reached far.
translations.idiomatic: To the south he awed Liang, to the north he won over the Rouran, and the Tuyuhun and Azhiluo were all brought in by his summons; he gained their strength for use — his design reached far.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
